author: Nancy Burns-Fusaro Sun staff writer
title: Stonington High School Drama to present 'Cinderella' this weekend | Entertainment | thewesterlysun.com
text:
STONINGTON — It was as if the entire Stonington High School auditorium was transported skyward Tuesday afternoon as the students on the stage — the young actors practicing their music for this weekend's performances of "Cinderella" — sang in beautiful harmony about "flying over mountain and meadow and glen."
"It's just so lovely," said Marla Ladd, the show's director, shortly before the students took to the stage for their first full dress rehearsal.
"The kids are great," she added, "and the parents are really supportive."
"It's the classic 1957 Rodgers & Hammerstein version," Ladd explained. "The one that was made for television and starred Julie Andrews as Cinderella."
In the Stonington High School Drama Club's version of the fairy tale, 16-year-old sophomore Zhena Robarge plays the role of Cinderella and has been enjoying every minute of the process.
"I love it," said Robarge with a bright smile as she sat in the cafeteria before the dress rehearsal between Jackson Ruenzel, who plays the Prince, and Alexa Checchi, who plays her Fairy Godmother. "We are having so much fun."
"I love hanging out with Alexa and rekindling my friendship with Jackson," she added.
"And I just love being her fairy godmother," put in Checchi, a 16-year-old junior who has been in a number of high school shows and is clearly relishing this role. "It's just so magical."
"And to be able to guide Cinderella on her journey" she added with excitement, "as I travel my own."
"I love acting," said Ruenzel, a 15-year-old freshman who said he was thrilled when he learned he landed the role of the leading man. "I like being on stage and I love my theater community here."
Checchi, who played a mean girl named Megan Jones in the school's fall production of "PUFFS, or Seven Increasingly Eventful Years at a Certain School of Magic and Magic," is clearly well-suited for the fairy godmother role.
As soon as Hannah Fyke, the co-stage manager for "Cinderella" — with Gracy Clerveaux — walked over to share some updates with the group, Checchi shared her flair for the dramatic.
"I love Hannah," she said, "She's my angel ... she and Gracy are angels walking on this earth."
They are making sure the show will be phenomenal, Checchi added with a smile.
While Robarge, Checchi and Ruenzel said juggling homework with rehearsal time was a bit of a challenge at the beginning of the process, they said they successfully conquered the time management challenge and are ready to take to the stage this weekend.
"The show really is magical," said Checchi as she stood to go to dress rehearsal, wearing her full petti-coated Fairy Godmother costume. "It's wonderful ... and impossible things happen."
"Tell everyone to come and see it," she added as she walked to the stage blowing kisses.
In the auditorium, 18-year-old senior Nora Fanning, who plays the role of the Stepmother, was smoothing her green gown and putting on her long, white gloves, when she paused to comment on the production.
"I really love what we've done with the set," she said.
"My favorite scene," she added, "is when I'm trying on the shoe and I have to hop around the stage on one foot."
With that, she hopped on stage to join the others who will be performing this weekend — Madison Oliverio, who plays the Queen; William Sundman, who plays the King; Julianna Matis, who plays Portia; Gwendolyn Fratoni-Jaskiewicz, Joy; Jackson Hine, Herald; Sophie Hryn, the Steward Gavin Prendergast, the Chef and ensemble members Emma Gowen, Natalia Lupinacci, Abby Cohen, Lauren deCastro and Cecelia Williams.
Along with Clerveaux and Fyke, the show's crew includes Thomas Berger, Sophia Orlowski, Mae Fanning, Shelby Stewart and Addison Galloway.
Although Robarge's Cinderella costume — which is handmade by Meredith Bogue — had not arrived by the time the dress rehearsal began, Robarge joined the others on stage as music director Chris Stanley began to play "Ten Minutes Ago."
"In the arms of my love, I’m flying," the students sang together. "Over mountain and meadow and glen, and I like it so well, that for all I can tell, I may never come down again. I may never come down to earth again."
